publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Indications & Usage

Lisinopril is indicated for the treatment of hypertension in adults and children >= 6 years; adjunct therapy in heart failure; acute myocardial infarction within 24 hours.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Dosage & Administration

Hypertension: Initial 10 mg once daily, titrate to 20-40 mg daily. Heart Failure: Initial 5 mg daily with diuretics. Acute MI: 5 mg within 24 hours, then 5 mg at 24h, 10 mg daily for 6 weeks.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Contraindications

History of angioedema with ACE inhibitor therapy, hereditary/idiopathic angioedema, concomitant aliskiren in diabetic patients.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Angioedema, anaphylaxis, hypotension in salt/volume depleted patients, renal impairment, hyperkalemia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Adverse Reactions

Dizziness, headache, persistent dry cough, fatigue, diarrhea, nausea, upper respiratory tract infection.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Drug Interactions

Diuretics: Additive hypotension. Potassium-sparing diuretics/potassium supplements: Hyperkalemia risk. NSAIDs: Renal dysfunction and reduced antihypertensive effect. Lithium: Toxicity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue Lisinopril as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Lisinopril - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Lisinopril
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Discontinue immediately (fetal toxicity). Renal impairment: Adjust dose when CrCl < 30 mL/min.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amlodipine - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Amlodipine
Section: Indications & Usage

Indicated for treatment of hypertension alone or in combination, and coronary artery disease (chronic stable angina and vasospastic angina).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amlodipine - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Amlodipine
Section: Dosage & Administration

Adults: 5 mg once daily, maximum 10 mg daily. Elderly/fragile/hepatic impairment: 2.5 mg once daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amlodipine - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Amlodipine
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity to amlodipine.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amlodipine - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Amlodipine
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Hypotension in severe aortic stenosis, worsening angina/MI on initiation in severe obstructive CAD, peripheral edema.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amlodipine - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Amlodipine
Section: Adverse Reactions

Peripheral edema (dose-dependent), dizziness, flushing, palpitations, fatigue, nausea, somnolence.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amlodipine - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Amlodipine
Section: Drug Interactions

Simvastatin: Limit simvastatin to 20 mg daily. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase amlodipine exposure. Cyclosporine/tacrolimus levels may increase.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amlodipine - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Amlodipine
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed. Hepatic impairment: Titrate slowly.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Indications & Usage

Hypertension, stroke risk reduction in hypertension and LV hypertrophy, diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes with elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Dosage & Administration

Hypertension: Initial 50 mg once daily (25 mg in volume-depleted or hepatic impairment), max 100 mg daily. Nephropathy: 50-100 mg once daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity; co-administration with aliskiren in diabetes.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Fetal toxicity, hypotension in volume-depleted patients, renal failure, hyperkalemia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Adverse Reactions

Upper respiratory infection, dizziness, nasal congestion, back pain, fatigue, hyperkalemia in diabetic renal disease.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Drug Interactions

Potassium-sparing diuretics/supplements: Hyperkalemia. NSAIDs: Renal impairment, decreased antihypertensive effect. Lithium: Toxicity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY. Discontinue Losartan immediately when pregnancy is detected. Renin-angiotensin blockers cause fetal injury, oligohydramnios, and death.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Losartan - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Losartan
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Contraindicated. Hepatic impairment: Start with 25 mg daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Indications & Usage

Treatment of essential hypertension; cardiovascular risk reduction in patients unable to take ACE inhibitors.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Dosage & Administration

Hypertension: Initial 40 mg once daily, titrate to 80 mg daily. CV Risk Reduction: 80 mg once daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity; concomitant aliskiren in diabetes.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Fetal toxicity, hypotension, hyperkalemia, impaired renal function.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Adverse Reactions

Sinusitis, back pain, diarrhea, pharyngitis, dizziness.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Drug Interactions

Digoxin: Increases peak digoxin levels. Lithium: Increases serum lithium. NSAIDs: Blunts antihypertensive effect, renal risk.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY. Discontinue Telmisartan as soon as pregnancy is detected (fetal toxicity and death).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Telmisartan - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Telmisartan
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Contraindicated.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Atorvastatin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Atorvastatin
Section: Indications & Usage

Adjunct to diet for primary hyperlipidemia, hypertriglyceridemia, prevention of cardiovascular disease (MI, stroke, revascularization) in patients at risk.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Atorvastatin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Atorvastatin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Initial 10 mg to 20 mg once daily; for > 45% LDL-C reduction start 40 mg once daily. Dose range 10-80 mg daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Atorvastatin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Atorvastatin
Section: Contraindications

Active liver disease, unexplained persistent transaminase elevation, pregnancy, lactation, hypersensitivity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Atorvastatin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Atorvastatin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure; immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy; liver enzyme elevations.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Atorvastatin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Atorvastatin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, extremity pain, UTI, dyspepsia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Atorvastatin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Atorvastatin
Section: Drug Interactions

Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole): Markedly increase rhabdomyolysis risk. Cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, fibrates: Increase myopathy risk.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Atorvastatin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Atorvastatin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy & Lactation: Contraindicated.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Rosuvastatin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Rosuvastatin
Section: Indications & Usage

Adjunct to diet in primary hyperlipidemia, mixed dyslipidemia, homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, and primary prevention of cardiovascular events.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Rosuvastatin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Rosuvastatin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Usual starting dose 10 mg to 20 mg once daily (5 mg in Asian ancestry or severe renal impairment). Maximum 40 mg daily (reserved for severe hypercholesterolemia).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Rosuvastatin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Rosuvastatin
Section: Contraindications

Active liver disease, pregnancy, lactation, hypersensitivity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Rosuvastatin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Rosuvastatin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Rhabdomyolysis, myopathy, proteinuria/hematuria at high doses, hepatic dysfunction, HbA1c elevation.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Rosuvastatin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Rosuvastatin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Headache, myalgia, abdominal pain, asthenia, nausea.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Rosuvastatin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Rosuvastatin
Section: Drug Interactions

Cyclosporine: 7-fold increase in rosuvastatin exposure (limit to 5 mg). Gemfibrozil: Avoid (limit to 10 mg). Protease inhibitors, antacids (take 2 hours after).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Rosuvastatin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Rosuvastatin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Asian ancestry: Initiate at 5 mg once daily due to 2-fold increased median exposure.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Indications & Usage

Hypertension, angina pectoris, stable symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class II or III) to reduce mortality and hospitalization.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Dosage & Administration

Hypertension: 25-100 mg once daily. Heart Failure: 12.5-25 mg once daily, titrating every 2 weeks up to 200 mg daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Contraindications

Severe bradycardia, 2nd or 3rd degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, decompensated heart failure, sick sinus syndrome.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Worsening heart failure on initiation, bronchospasm in reactive airway disease, masking hypoglycemia symptoms, bradycardia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Adverse Reactions

Dizziness, fatigue, bradycardia, depression, shortness of breath, diarrhea, hypotension.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Drug Interactions

CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine, diphenhydramine): Increase metoprolol levels. Calcium channel blockers (verapamil, diltiazem): Additive bradycardia and AV block. Digoxin.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: ISCHEMIC HEART DISEASE RISK ON ABRUPT CESSATION. Do not abruptly discontinue Metoprolol in patients with CAD. Severe exacerbation of angina, MI, and ventricular arrhythmias have been reported after abrupt cessation. Taper over 1 to 2 weeks.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metoprolol Succinate - Use in Specific Populations
focus: Metoprolol Succinate - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Metoprolol Succinate
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Fetal bradycardia and hypoglycemia risk.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Hydrochlorothiazide - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Hydrochlorothiazide
Section: Indications & Usage

Adjunctive therapy in edema associated with heart failure, cirrhosis, corticosteroid therapy; management of hypertension alone or in combination.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Hydrochlorothiazide - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Hydrochlorothiazide
Section: Dosage & Administration

Hypertension: Initial 12.5 mg to 25 mg once daily; max 50 mg daily. Edema: 25 mg to 100 mg daily in single or divided doses.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Hydrochlorothiazide - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Hydrochlorothiazide
Section: Contraindications

Anuria, hypersensitivity to hydrochlorothiazide or sulfonamide-derived drugs.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Hydrochlorothiazide - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Hydrochlorothiazide
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypomagnesemic alkalosis, hyperuricemia (precipitating acute gout), hyperglycemia in diabetes, acute angle-closure glaucoma.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Hydrochlorothiazide - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Hydrochlorothiazide
Section: Adverse Reactions

Hypokalemia, hyperuricemia, dizziness, vertigo, orthostatic hypotension, photosensitivity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Hydrochlorothiazide - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Hydrochlorothiazide
Section: Drug Interactions

Lithium: Decreased renal clearance leading to lithium toxicity. NSAIDs: Reduce diuretic effect. Antidiabetic agents: Dosage adjustment may be needed.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Hydrochlorothiazide - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Hydrochlorothiazide
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Renal Impairment: Ineffective when CrCl < 30 mL/min.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Indications & Usage

Treatment of edema associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and renal disease (including nephrotic syndrome); hypertension alone or with other antihypertensives.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Dosage & Administration

Edema: Initial 20 mg to 80 mg single dose; titrate in 20-40 mg increments every 6-8 hours. Maintenance dose up to 600 mg/day in severe refractory edema.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Contraindications

Anuria; hypersensitivity to furosemide.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Profound fluid loss, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, ototoxicity (especially with rapid IV injection or concomitant aminoglycosides), hyperuricemia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Adverse Reactions

Dehydration, electrolyte depletion, orthostatic hypotension, tinnitus, hearing loss, hyperuricemia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Drug Interactions

Aminoglycosides (gentamicin, amikacin): Synergistic ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Digoxin: Hypokalemia potentiates digitalis arrhythmias. Lithium: Toxicity. NSAIDs: Antagonize diuretic effect.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: PROFOUND DIURESIS AND ELECTROLYTE DEPLETION. Furosemide is a potent diuretic that, if given in excessive amounts, can lead to profound diuresis with water and electrolyte depletion. Careful medical supervision and individualized dose schedule are required.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Furosemide - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Furosemide
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Geriatric: Monitor electrolytes and renal function closely.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Indications & Usage

Acute Coronary Syndrome (unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI); recent MI, recent ischemic stroke, or established peripheral arterial disease.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Dosage & Administration

Acute Coronary Syndrome: 300 mg oral loading dose, then 75 mg once daily with aspirin (75-325 mg daily). Recent MI/Stroke/PAD: 75 mg once daily without loading dose.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Contraindications

Active pathological bleeding (e.g. peptic ulcer or intracranial hemorrhage); hypersensitivity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Bleeding risk: Discontinue 5 days prior to elective surgery. Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) reported rarely. CYP2C19 poor metabolizers.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Adverse Reactions

Bleeding, purpura, bruising, epistaxis, hematoma, gastrointestinal hemorrhage.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Drug Interactions

CYP2C19 Inhibitors (omeprazole, esomeprazole): Significantly reduce clopidogrel active metabolite and antiplatelet efficacy; avoid concomitant use. Anticoagulants (warfarin, apixaban) / NSAIDs: Increased major bleeding risk.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: DIMINISHED ANTIPLATELET EFFECT IN CYP2C19 POOR METABOLIZERS. The effectiveness of Clopidogrel depends on its activation to an active metabolite by the cytochrome P450 (CYP) system, principally CYP2C19. Poor metabolizers exhibit higher rates of cardiovascular events (stent thrombosis, MI) following acute coronary syndrome or PCI.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Clopidogrel - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Clopidogrel
Section: Use in Specific Populations

CYP2C19 poor metabolizers: Consider alternative P2Y12 inhibitors (prasugrel, ticagrelor).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Indications & Usage

Prophylaxis and treatment of venous thromboembolism, pulmonary embolism, thromboembolic complications associated with atrial fibrillation or cardiac valve replacement.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Target INR 2.0 to 3.0 (2.5 to 3.5 in mechanical prosthetic valves). Initial 2-5 mg once daily, adjust according to INR.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Contraindications

Pregnancy (major teratogen), active bleeding, hemorrhagic tendencies, recent eye/brain surgery, severe uncontrolled hypertension.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Major hemorrhage, tissue necrosis and gangrene, calciphylaxis, systemic atheroemboli.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Fatal and nonfatal hemorrhage, tissue necrosis, purpura, elevated liver enzymes.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Drug Interactions

Aspirin/NSAIDs: Dramatically increase GI and major bleeding risk. CYP2C9 inhibitors (fluconazole, metronidazole, amiodarone): Markedly increase INR and bleeding risk. CYP2C9 inducers (rifampin): Decrease INR.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: BLEEDING RISK. Warfarin sodium can cause major or fatal bleeding. Perform regular monitoring of INR in all treated patients. Numerous factors including diet, medications, and botanical products influence INR.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Warfarin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Warfarin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Strictly contraindicated (Warfarin Embryopathy).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Indications & Usage

Reduction of risk of stroke and systemic embolism in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation; DVT/PE prophylaxis in knee/hip replacement; treatment of DVT and PE; reduction in the risk of recurrent DVT and PE.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Dosage & Administration

Nonvalvular AF: 5 mg twice daily. Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily if patient has at least 2 of: Age >= 80 years, Body weight <= 60 kg, Serum creatinine >= 1.5 mg/dL. DVT/PE Treatment: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Contraindications

Active pathological bleeding; severe hypersensitivity to apixaban.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Bleeding risk; prosthetic heart valves (not recommended); spinal/epidural anesthesia hematoma.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Adverse Reactions

Major bleeding, epistaxis, hematuria, gingival bleeding, contusion, anemia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Drug Interactions

Dual strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir): Reduce apixaban dose by 50% or avoid. Dual inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine): Avoid concomitant use. Antiplatelet agents / NSAIDs: Increased bleeding risk.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: PREMATURE DISCONTINUATION INCREASES RISK OF THROMBOTIC EVENTS; SPINAL/EPIDURAL HEMATOMA. Premature discontinuation of any oral anticoagulant increases the risk of thrombotic events. Epidural or spinal hematomas may occur in patients who are anticoagulated with apixaban receiving neuraxial anesthesia or spinal puncture.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Apixaban - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Apixaban
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Renal Impairment: Dose reduction criteria applies for AF.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Indications & Usage

First-line pharmacological therapy as adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Initial 500 mg twice daily or 850 mg once daily with meals. Increase to max 2000-2550 mg daily in divided doses. eGFR < 30 mL/min: Contraindicated; eGFR 30-45 mL/min: Max 1000 mg/day.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Contraindications

Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2), metabolic acidosis, acute or chronic DKA.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Lactic acidosis, iodinated contrast imaging (hold metformin), Vitamin B12 deficiency (monitor every 2-3 years).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, flatulence, abdominal pain, asthenia, metallic taste.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Drug Interactions

Alcohol: Potentiates lactate metabolism and acidosis risk. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors: Increase acidosis. Cationic drugs.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS. Metformin-associated lactic acidosis is a serious, rare, and potentially fatal metabolic complication. Risk factors include renal impairment, concomitant drugs, age >= 65, radiocontrast studies, hypoxia, and alcohol abuse.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Metformin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Metformin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Renal Impairment: Contraindicated in eGFR < 30 mL/min.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Glimepiride - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Glimepiride
Section: Indications & Usage

Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Glimepiride - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Glimepiride
Section: Dosage & Administration

Initial starting dose is 1 mg to 2 mg once daily with breakfast. Titrate in 1-2 mg increments every 1 to 2 weeks up to maximum 8 mg once daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Glimepiride - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Glimepiride
Section: Contraindications

Known hypersensitivity to glimepiride or other sulfonylureas or sulfonamides.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Glimepiride - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Glimepiride
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Hypoglycemia: Severe and prolonged hypoglycemia can occur, especially in elderly, debilitated, malnourished, or renal impairment. Hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Glimepiride - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Glimepiride
Section: Adverse Reactions

Hypoglycemia, dizziness, asthenia, headache, nausea, allergic skin reactions, weight gain.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Glimepiride - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Glimepiride
Section: Drug Interactions

NSAIDs, fluconazole, clarithromycin, sulfonamides: Potentiate hypoglycemic action. Beta-blockers: Mask hypoglycemic tachycardia and tremors.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Glimepiride - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Glimepiride
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Renal Impairment: Start at 1 mg once daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Empagliflozin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Empagliflozin
Section: Indications & Usage

Glycemic control in type 2 diabetes; reduction of cardiovascular death risk in adults with T2DM and established CVD; reduction of cardiovascular death and hospitalization in heart failure (HFrEF and HFpEF); reduction of chronic kidney disease progression.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Empagliflozin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Empagliflozin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Recommended starting dose is 10 mg once daily in the morning with or without food; may increase to 25 mg once daily. eGFR < 20 mL/min: Not recommended.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Empagliflozin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Empagliflozin
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity; patients on dialysis.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Empagliflozin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Empagliflozin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Diabetic Ketoacidosis (Euglycemic DKA): Can occur with normal blood glucose levels; withhold empagliflozin prior to surgery. Volume depletion and hypotension. Urosepsis and Pyelonephritis. Fournier's Gangrene (necrotizing fasciitis of perineum). Genital mycotic infections.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Empagliflozin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Empagliflozin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Urinary tract infections, female genital mycotic infections, polyuria, dyslipidemia, thirst.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Empagliflozin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Empagliflozin
Section: Drug Interactions

Diuretics: Additive volume depletion and hypotension. Insulin / Insulin secretagogues: Increased risk of hypoglycemia (lower insulin dose).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Empagliflozin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Empagliflozin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Not recommended in 2nd and 3rd trimesters due to potential risk to fetal kidney development.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Sitagliptin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Sitagliptin
Section: Indications & Usage

Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Sitagliptin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Sitagliptin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Usual dose is 100 mg once daily with or without food. Moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30 to < 45): 50 mg once daily. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 or ESRD/dialysis): 25 mg once daily.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Sitagliptin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Sitagliptin
Section: Contraindications

History of serious hypersensitivity reaction (anaphylaxis, angioedema) to sitagliptin.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Sitagliptin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Sitagliptin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Acute Pancreatitis: Including fatal and nonfatal hemorrhagic or necrotizing pancreatitis; discontinue immediately if suspected. Heart Failure risk. Severe and disabling arthralgia. Bullous Pemphigoid.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Sitagliptin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Sitagliptin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Upper respiratory tract infection, nasopharyngitis, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Sitagliptin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Sitagliptin
Section: Drug Interactions

Digoxin: Slight increase in digoxin AUC (monitor patients on digoxin). Sulfonylureas/Insulin: Reduce secretagogue dose to prevent hypoglycemia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Sitagliptin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Sitagliptin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Renal Impairment: Dose adjustment based on eGFR.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amoxicillin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Amoxicillin
Section: Indications & Usage

Infections of ear, nose, throat (otitis media, sinusitis), lower respiratory tract (CAP), genitourinary tract, skin/skin structure due to susceptible organisms; H. pylori eradication.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amoxicillin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Amoxicillin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Adults: 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours. Severe CAP: 875 mg every 12 hours.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amoxicillin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Amoxicillin
Section: Contraindications

Serious hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) to amoxicillin or other penicillins.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amoxicillin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Amoxicillin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Anaphylaxis, Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD), development of drug-resistant bacteria.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amoxicillin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Amoxicillin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, urticaria, elevated transaminases.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amoxicillin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Amoxicillin
Section: Drug Interactions

Methotrexate: Reduces renal clearance of methotrexate leading to toxicity. Allopurinol: High rate of skin rash. Warfarin.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Amoxicillin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Amoxicillin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Category B (safe in pregnancy).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Azithromycin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Azithromycin
Section: Indications & Usage

Community-acquired pneumonia, acute bacterial exacerbations of COPD, acute sinusitis, pharyngitis, skin infections, urethritis/cervicitis due to Chlamydia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Azithromycin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Azithromycin
Section: Dosage & Administration

CAP / Skin / Pharyngitis: 500 mg Day 1, then 250 mg once daily Days 2-5. Acute COPD / Sinusitis: 500 mg once daily for 3 days. Chlamydia: 1 g single dose.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Azithromycin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Azithromycin
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity to macrolides; history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with prior azithromycin.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Azithromycin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Azithromycin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

QT Prolongation and Torsades de Pointes ventricular arrhythmia; hepatotoxicity; CDAD.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Azithromycin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Azithromycin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, dizziness.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Azithromycin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Azithromycin
Section: Drug Interactions

QT-prolonging drugs (amiodarone, quinidine, fluoroquinolones): Fatal arrhythmia risk. Antacids reduce peak absorption. Digoxin.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Azithromycin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Azithromycin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Hepatic Impairment: Biliary excretion; use with caution.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ceftriaxone - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Ceftriaxone
Section: Indications & Usage

Lower respiratory tract infections (pneumonia), acute bacterial otitis media, skin/skin structure infections, urinary tract infections, gonorrhea, pelvic inflammatory disease, bacterial septicemia, bone/joint infections, intra-abdominal infections, meningitis.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ceftriaxone - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Ceftriaxone
Section: Dosage & Administration

Adults: 1 g to 2 g IV or IM once daily (or divided twice daily) depending on severity. Meningitis: 2 g IV every 12 hours. Gonorrhea: 500 mg IM single dose.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ceftriaxone - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Ceftriaxone
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity to cephalosporins. Premature neonates up to 41 weeks post-menstrual age. Hyperbilirubinemic neonates. Neonates (<= 28 days) requiring calcium-containing IV solutions (fatal ceftriaxone-calcium precipitation).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ceftriaxone - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Ceftriaxone
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Hypersensitivity / anaphylaxis; CDAD; biliary sludging (pseudolithiasis); hemolytic anemia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ceftriaxone - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Ceftriaxone
Section: Adverse Reactions

Diarrhea, eosinophilia, thrombocytosis, elevated AST/ALT, local site pain/phlebitis.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ceftriaxone - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Ceftriaxone
Section: Drug Interactions

Calcium-containing solutions (e.g. Ringer's or Hartmann's): Precipitation risk in neonates and lung/kidney autopsy findings. Warfarin: Increased INR.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ceftriaxone - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Ceftriaxone
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Neonates: Contraindicated with calcium IV solutions.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Indications & Usage

Complicated urinary tract infections, pyelonephritis, infectious diarrhea, typhoid fever, bone and joint infections, complicated intra-abdominal infections (with metronidazole), anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis. Reserved for use when no alternative options exist in acute sinusitis, bronchitis, or uncomplicated cystitis.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Adults: 250 mg to 750 mg orally every 12 hours. Complicated UTI / Pyelonephritis: 500 mg twice daily for 7-14 days.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity to fluoroquinolones; concomitant administration with tizanidine.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Tendon rupture (Achilles), peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects (seizures, hallucinations, depression), aortic aneurysm and dissection, QT prolongation.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Nausea, diarrhea, elevated transaminases, vomiting, rash, headache, insomnia.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Drug Interactions

Tizanidine: Severe hypotension and sedation (contraindicated). Multivalent cations (antacids, iron, calcium, magnesium): Markedly reduce ciprofloxacin absorption (separate by 2h before / 6h after). Theophylline: Significant elevation of theophylline levels and seizure risk. Warfarin.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: SERIOUS ADVERSE REACTIONS INCLUDING TENDINITIS, TENDON RUPTURE, PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY, CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM EFFECTS AND EXACERBATION OF MYASTHENIA GRAVIS. Fluoroquinolones are associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions that have occurred together.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ciprofloxacin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Ciprofloxacin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pediatric & Pregnancy: Avoid unless treating inhalational anthrax or complicated UTI due to cartilage arthropathy risks.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Doxycycline - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Doxycycline
Section: Indications & Usage

Rickettsial infections (Rocky Mountain spotted fever, scrub typhus, Q fever); atypical pneumonia (Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae); cholera; Lyme disease; malaria prophylaxis; acne vulgaris; pelvic inflammatory disease.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Doxycycline - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Doxycycline
Section: Dosage & Administration

Adults: 100 mg every 12 hours on Day 1, followed by 100 mg once daily or 100 mg twice daily for severe infections. Administer with adequate fluids to prevent esophageal ulceration.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Doxycycline - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Doxycycline
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity to doxycycline or other tetracyclines.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Doxycycline - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Doxycycline
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy, children under 8 years); photosensitivity; intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri); esophageal irritation.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Doxycycline - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Doxycycline
Section: Adverse Reactions

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, photosensitivity skin rash, esophageal ulceration, elevated BUN.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Doxycycline - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Doxycycline
Section: Drug Interactions

Antacids (aluminum, calcium, magnesium), iron preparations, bismuth subsalicylate: Impair doxycycline absorption. Oral Contraceptives: Reduced effectiveness. Warfarin: Potentiates anticoagulant effect.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Doxycycline - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Doxycycline
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy & Children < 8 years: Tooth staining and bone growth inhibition (avoid unless life-threatening conditions like anthrax or scrub typhus).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Aspirin - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Aspirin
Section: Indications & Usage

Secondary prevention of cardiovascular events in established CAD, previous MI, or ischemic stroke; temporary relief of minor pain, headache, and fever reduction.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Aspirin - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Aspirin
Section: Dosage & Administration

Cardioprotection (low-dose): 75 mg to 100 mg (typically 81 mg) once daily. Acute MI: 162-325 mg chewed immediately. Analgesia: 325-650 mg every 4-6h (max 4000 mg/day).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Aspirin - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Aspirin
Section: Contraindications

Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (aspirin triad: asthma, nasal polyps, rhinitis); active peptic ulcer; bleeding disorders; children/teens with viral infections (Reye's syndrome).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Aspirin - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Aspirin
Section: Warnings & Precautions

GI bleeding, ulceration, Reye's syndrome in pediatrics, renal impairment, tinnitus in salicylate toxicity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Aspirin - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Aspirin
Section: Adverse Reactions

Dyspepsia, heartburn, epigastric pain, occult bleeding, prolonged bleeding time.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Aspirin - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Aspirin
Section: Drug Interactions

Anticoagulants (warfarin, heparin, apixaban): Major synergistic bleeding risk. NSAIDs (ibuprofen): Interferes with antiplatelet action and increases GI toxicity. Methotrexate: Severe toxicity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Aspirin - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Aspirin
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pediatric: Contraindicated in viral illness (Reye's syndrome). Pregnancy: Avoid in 3rd trimester.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Indications & Usage

Relief of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, mild to moderate pain, reduction of fever, dysmenorrhea.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Dosage & Administration

Adults: 400 mg to 800 mg every 6 to 8 hours (max 3200 mg daily). Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Contraindications

Hypersensitivity to ibuprofen or aspirin; history of asthma/urticaria with NSAIDs; CABG surgery setting.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Cardiovascular thrombotic risk, GI ulceration/bleeding, acute renal failure, hypertension, heart failure edema.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Adverse Reactions

Nausea, epigastric pain, heartburn, dizziness, edema, tinnitus.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Drug Interactions

Aspirin: Interferes with cardioprotection and increases GI risk. Anticoagulants (warfarin): Massive bleeding risk. ACE Inhibitors / ARBs: Renal toxicity, blunted BP response. Lithium: Increases lithium.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: CARDIOVASCULAR AND GASTROINTESTINAL RISK. NSAIDs cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events (MI and stroke) and serious gastrointestinal adverse events (bleeding, ulceration, perforation) which can be fatal. Contraindicated in CABG surgery.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Ibuprofen - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Ibuprofen
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Avoid from 20 weeks onward (oligohydramnios / premature ductus closure).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Indications & Usage

Temporary relief of minor aches and pains (headache, arthritis, backache, toothache, cold) and reduction of fever.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Dosage & Administration

Adults: 325 mg to 650 mg every 4-6 hours or 1000 mg every 6 hours (max 4000 mg in 24 hours; recommended max 3000 mg/day in elderly/chronic use).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Contraindications

Severe active liver disease or severe hepatic impairment; hypersensitivity.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Hepatotoxicity, serious skin reactions (SJS, TEN). Check all OTC/Rx combination medications for duplicate acetaminophen.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Adverse Reactions

Generally well-tolerated; rash, pruritus, severe hepatic necrosis in overdose.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Drug Interactions

Alcohol: Chronic consumption markedly increases hepatotoxicity risk through CYP2E1 induction. Warfarin: Prolonged high doses (> 2g/day) may elevate INR.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY. Acetaminophen has been associated with cases of acute liver failure, sometimes requiring transplant or resulting in death. Overdose occurs with > 4000 mg/day or combining multiple products.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Paracetamol - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Paracetamol
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pregnancy: Antipyretic/analgesic of choice in pregnancy at lowest effective dose.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Indications & Usage
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Indications & Usage

Management of moderate to severe pain in adults severe enough to require an opioid analgesic when alternative treatments are inadequate.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Dosage & Administration
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Dosage & Administration

Initial 25 mg to 50 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum daily dose is 400 mg/day (300 mg/day in patients > 75 years).

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Contraindications
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Contraindications

Children under 12 years; post-operative management in pediatric tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy; significant respiratory depression; acute or severe bronchial asthma; concurrent MAOI use.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Warnings & Precautions
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Warnings & Precautions

Seizure risk (especially with SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, or history of epilepsy); Serotonin Syndrome; respiratory depression; suicide risk; opioid withdrawal.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Adverse Reactions
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Adverse Reactions

Dizziness, nausea, constipation, somnolence, headache, vomiting, pruritus, sweating.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Drug Interactions
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Drug Interactions

SSRIs / SNRIs / TCAs / Triptans: Severe risk of life-threatening Serotonin Syndrome and seizures. Benzodiazepines / CNS depressants: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death. MAO Inhibitors.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Boxed Warning
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Boxed Warning

WARNING: ADDICTION, ABUSE, AND MISUSE; RISK OF SERIOUS RESPIRATORY DEPRESSION; ACCIDENTAL INGESTION; ULTRA-RAPID METABOLISM OF TRAMADOL AND OTHER RISK FACTORS FOR LIFE-THREATENING RESPIRATORY DEPRESSION IN CHILDREN; INTERACTIONS WITH BENZODIAZEPINES AND OTHER CNS DEPRESSANTS.

publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA
title: Tramadol - Use in Specific Populations
text:
Drug: Tramadol
Section: Use in Specific Populations

Pediatric: Contraindicated under 12 years. Lactation: Contraindicated in breastfeeding due to rapid CYP2D6 metabolism risk.
